title: The Detective
build: T64 tape image of a cracked release: the game packed into one 44,302-byte program (Trianon, 1987), and a second program of crackers' instructions (Danish Gold, 1987)

records.c: The processor port's direction register; the warm start writes $2F to it.
The processor port: $35 in play (all RAM, I/O at $D000), $34 while a room picture is unpacked, $36 while the keyboard is read.

The rectangles of the room objects the player cannot walk through, one byte per object number (the values in $0250): $1B00 and $1B20 the first and last column, $1B40 and $1B60 the nearest and farthest depth; read by $2EB4
Last column of each object's rectangle.
Nearest depth of each object's rectangle.
Farthest depth of each object's rectangle.

Room tables, one byte for each of 32 rooms: here the room's first multicolour ($5D, for $D022), then at $1BA0 its second ($5E, $D023), $1BC0 its type (bit 7: the picture is widened), $1BE0 its depth ($02A7), $1C00 the depth of its front edge ($C4), $1C20 its width in columns; read by build_room ($388D)
The room's second multicolour, for $D022's partner $D023.
The room's type (bits 0-6: picture record, hook and sounds; bit 7: widen the picture).
The room's depth from the back wall.
The depth of the room's front edge.
The room's width in columns of the room map.

The objects of each room, a list per room in room order, each ended by a negative byte ($2F5E reads them); some entries are changed in play: the safe ($8AC2) and the bodies ($AC96, $ACEC, $B19E, $B1CF)
An entry of the room object lists ($1C40), cleared at the start of a game ($86CA) and by the safe ($8AC7).
Part of room_object_lists ($1C40), read by $86CD, $8ACA.
Part of room_object_lists ($1C40), read by $86D9.
An entry of the room object lists ($1C40), cleared at the start of a game ($86D0) and set when Cynthia dies ($AC9A).
An entry of the room object lists ($1C40), cleared at the start of a game ($86DC) and set when Gabriel dies ($AD12).
Part of room_object_lists ($1C40), read by $86D6, $B1E2.
Part of room_object_lists ($1C40), read by $86D3, $B1AC.
Which of the three room character sets each room uses (0-2), read by build_room through $3CC0

The 32 door records, eight bytes each: the room on one side (+0) and the door's place there (+1), the room on the other side (+2) and its place (+3), the flags (+4: bit 0 open, bit 1 locked), each side's door type and position bits (+5, +6), and the object that is its key (+7)
A door record's +1: the door's place in the room at +0.
A door record's +2: the room on the other side.
A door record's +3: the door's place in the room at +2.
A door record's +4: its flags, bit 0 open, bit 1 locked.
A door record's +5: the door's type and position bits on the side of the room at +0.
A door record's +6: the door's type and position bits on the side of the room at +2.
Part of doors ($1F00), read by $3EC1.
Door 2's flags, set to locked at the start of a game by $86E4.
Door 3's flags (+4 of its record), set to locked at the start of a game by $86E7.
Door 20's flags, set to locked at the start of a game by $86EA.

The engine's jump table: 24 three-byte JMPs at $2000-$2047, the entry points the adventure module at $8000 calls. $2000 is the start-up, and also where the loader's last stage lands and where the cartridge-style vectors at $8000 point.
Engine jump table entry: draw_icons ($32CE).
Engine jump table entry: irq_room_end ($2A68).
Engine jump table entry: print_ay ($21C6).
Engine jump table entry: door_open_close ($3E9D).
Engine jump table entry: door_unlock ($3EB8).
Engine jump table entry: print_inline ($28DE).
Engine jump table entry: row_address ($2419).
Engine jump table entry: build_room ($388D).
Engine jump table entry: read_joystick ($2200).
Engine jump table entry: lights_out ($2696).
Engine jump table entry: place_cast_end ($3722).

Cold start, run once from the loader's jump to $2000. Clears the whole of zero page (STA $02,X with X counting down from 0 wraps within the page, reaching $00 and $01) and the stack page, then $3FF0-$3FF9 and $3FFF, and falls into the warm start at $2067.

Warm start, also reached from the NMI handler when RESTORE is pressed in play. Resets the stack, blanks the screen, sets $01 to $35 (RAM everywhere, I/O visible), video bank 1, initialises video, sound, the adventure module ($8024) and the interrupts, runs the title sequence ($222D) and then sets up a new game: clock strings from $2153/$2158, the cast's starting places ($8054, $8057), and enters the task loop at $2120.
Inside the warm start; the address is named only as the operand of a BIT at $279D that skips a LDA #$E9.
The main loop: calls the ten tasks of the table at $213F in turn, for ever, each through JMP ($26) at $213C.
JMP ($26): calls the task whose address the loop put in $26/$27.
The main loop's ten tasks, in the order run: fire latch test ($2224), joystick read ($2200), then $8033, $3E49, $2EB4, $378A, $803C, $804B, $2592 and $3979.
Part of task_table ($213F), read by $212B.
"09:10", copied to $1EBD at the start of a game.
"11:03", copied to $1EC4 at the start of a game.
"INTRODUCING THE CAST..", printed by the title sequence before the cast's biographies.

Turns all sprites off and unexpanded, sets the border and background to black and every sprite behind the background ($D01B = $FF), keeps the screen-on bit of $D011 with text mode, sets $D016 = $10 (multicolour, 38 columns) and $D018 = $F0 (screen $7C00, characters $4000 in bank 1).
Clears all SID registers, waits a short delay loop, then sets the volume to 10.
Prints the zero-terminated string at A (high) / Y (low) through print_char ($21D8). Entry $21CA prints the string at ($26).

Puts one character into the text line buffer: a byte below $60 is stored at $0400 + the column in $012D, which then advances. A byte of $60 or more is a word token: its low five bits go in X to the adventure module's token printer ($806F), with $26/$27 and Y saved round the call. A, X and the flags are preserved for the plain case.

Reads joystick port 2 ($DC00) until two reads agree, flips the fire bit so that 1 means pressed, and shifts left three times: fire ends in bit 7. Keeps the result in $4B and sets the latch $0129 to $80 when fire has gone from released to pressed since the last read. Returns the latch in A.
Tests the fire latch $0129: N set if fire was pressed since the last test, then clears the latch.

The title screen: writes the copyright line from $22E3 (converted to screen codes) to row 1 of the screen, makes sure the title's character set is the one at $4000 (swapping the two sets with $22BE if the first byte of $4000 is not $3C), copies sprite pointers and positions from $234A-$2361 to $0208-$021F, calls $23A8 and the adventure module's $8018 with interrupts off, turns the screen on, and waits for fire. While it waits it calls $8039 once when the counter $1E66 reaches 21 and $2741 when it then reaches 27. On fire it blanks the screen, sets the game state $0F to 2, calls $26F5, and falls into swap_charsets, which puts the game's character set back at $4000.
Swaps the 2 KB at $4000-$47FF with the 2 KB at $EA00-$F1FF, with interrupts off: the title's character set and the game's change places.

The copyright line for the title, in the title set's own codes: byte $00 is the copyright sign (glyph 0 of the title set), then " A.P.S. SOFTWARE 1986" with each full stop stored as $5C; title_sequence ($222F) converts the line to screen codes, $5C becoming $3C.
Clears the eight entries of each per-sprite table at $0208, $0210, $0218, $0220, $0238 and $0248.
Sets the colour of screen rows 0-14 (colour RAM through the row table) to 11, dark grey: the room's part of the screen.
Draws the title's picture box: twelve characters from $233E on row 12 from column 13 ($7DED), in white, and character $0B at row 13 column 22 ($7E1E), also white.
Twelve character codes for the title's box ($2325).
Start values for the title's eight sprites, copied by the title routine: eight X positions (to $0208), eight X high bytes (to $0210) and eight Y positions (to $0218).
Part of title_sprite_init ($234A), read by $2259.
Part of title_sprite_init ($234A), read by $225F.
Moves the title's eight sprites up the screen: every third call adds 1 to each Y position at $0218 and wraps it to 0 at $AA. Reached through the address at $2C24.
Builds the 256-byte table at $0500 that reverses the order of the four two-bit pixels of a multicolour byte (a picture flipped left to right), calls $801E, and clears the sprite shape at $7BC0-$7BFF.

Fills the title's logo area with character codes counting up from $40, 24 columns a row from row 3 column 8 ($7C80), skipping one column of rows past code $70, in light blue; when the codes reach $FA it places the six codes $FA-$FF by hand at $7CE2-$7D5B.
Fills all 25 rows of the screen at $7C00 with spaces.
LDX #$00 just before row_address ($2419): no instruction jumps or calls here; perhaps the start of a routine for row 0 that lost its callers.
Sets $D1/$D2 to the screen address of row X (tables $244A/$2464) and falls into $2423.
Sets $F3/$F4 to the colour RAM address that matches the screen address in $D1/$D2.
X = the text cursor's row $33 plus 17: the screen row of the text panel's line.
Sets $57/$58 and $59 to the screen address of row X, and $5A to its colour RAM page.
Low bytes of the screen address of rows 0-25 (screen $7C00, 40 bytes a row).
High bytes of the screen address of rows 0-25, and one more byte.
Moves $D1/$D2 on by one row (40 bytes) and recomputes the colour pointer.
Moves $D1/$D2 back by one row and recomputes the colour pointer.
Clears screen rows 15 and 16 ($7E58-$7EA7) to spaces in white: the two lines under the room.
Takes its return address as a pointer to a zero-terminated string, prints it through print_ay ($21C6) and returns past it. No instruction in the image calls it.
Shows sprite 4 at X (low), Y and the X high bits in A, multicolour, with shape $D6 ($7580); its colour steps through the 16 colours at $34D9 as the counter $026F goes up on each call.
When the room $C7 is 14 and the low two bits of $1E68 are not zero, writes character $9D into the room buffer at $1500 plus one of the offsets 9, 14 or 19 ($2508) chosen by those bits.
Three offsets into the buffer at $1500, indexed 1-3 by $24F1.

Places a character's two sprites by the shape type in A: 1, side by side (the second 24 pixels right), both at the character's Y plus 21; 2, one above the other (the second 2 pixels left and 21 lines up); 3, one sprite at line $92 and the second off the screen. Other types go to $2A4D.
Adds one minute to the clock string at $1EBD ("HH:MM"), carrying through the digits with the limits at $258D.
The digit after the largest each place of the clock may hold: hours tens and units, the colon (skipped), minutes tens and units.

A main-loop task. Unless $1BC0 is 3 or $1B is 4 or more, compares the clock at $1EBD with the time limit at $1EC4 and, once it is reached, puts out the lights ($2696), calls $806C with 3, prints "<you> ARE SHOT BY AN UNSEEN ASSASIN" ($2639) and ends the game ($25BF).

Turns the volume up, plays three bursts of noise on voice 1 ($25FE), falls into $25D6, sets the game state $0F to 2, prints "THE GAME IS OVER." ($265B), calls $806C with 6 and restarts at the warm start.
Sets $1EA5 to 1 and $1D91/$1D9B to $D7/$D8 and the volume to 14. Also reached through the jump table at $2033.
Counts the game in $49, sets state 2, prints "THE GAME IS OVER.", calls $806C with 6 and restarts at the warm start. Also reached through $203F.
One burst on voice 1: frequency high byte $70, attack 0 decay 1, sustain 9 release 6, noise waveform gated on for a short delay, off, and silenced after a longer one.
A delay loop of X times 256 times 63 counts.

" ARE SHOT BY AN UNSEEN ASSASIN

", with word tokens $6B and $70.
"THE GAME IS OVER."
"THE LIGHTS GO OUT" and word token $70.
Game state handler 9 (table $2B0F): sets state 9 and clears screen rows 0-14.
Sets the game state $0F to 1 and prints "THE LIGHTS GO OUT". Reached through the jump table at $203C and from the time limit.

Sets the X high bit (bit 8) of the sprite the index Y points at in $B3, from the carry of A shifted right, for the sprite pair's second sprite (entry $26A1) or first ($26A3), and returns Y rounded down to a multiple of 4.
An entry into sprite_x_high ($26A1), reached from $2547.
The eight single-bit masks $01-$80.
Resets the text panel: cursor at line 0 column 1, clears screen rows 17-24 in columns 0-23, and the more-counter $026E.
Starts the text panel's fade-in: $5B = 5 steps, cursor home.
One step of the panel's fade-in, every fourth call: sets the colour of the panel's lines from the table at $273C, and at the last step clears the panel.
Panel colours for the fade-in steps.
Clears and fades in the text panel, then returns through $27ED. Printing a "*" does the same.

Prints the character in A at the text panel's cursor, keeping A, X, Y and the flags. Waits for any fade to finish, then: carriage return starts a new line; "*" clears the panel; letters ($40 and up) have $20 taken off (the SBC #$20 hidden in the BIT at $279D) to make the panel font's codes; punctuation and digits are mapped to the panel font's codes one by one. After the seventh line it waits for fire once every six lines (a "more" pause) and asks the interrupt to scroll the panel up ($56).
Restores A, X, Y and the flags saved by $2800 and returns.
Saves A, X, Y and the flags in $014B-$014E.
Called from the interrupt: steps the fade, blinks the cursor (colours from $288E and $2896 on the cursor's row), scrolls the panel up one line when $56 asks, and in game state 6 goes on to $8060.
Character codes for the blinking cursor's eight steps.
Colours for the blinking cursor's eight steps.

Prints the zero-terminated text at A (high) / Y (low) in the text panel, a word at a time, starting a new line when the next word would go past column 24. Words end at a space, comma, carriage return or the zero. Entry $28A2 prints the text at ($26).
Reads the next character of the text: carry set at the end (zero), clear at a space, comma or carriage return, with Y moved on.
Takes its return address as a pointer to a zero-terminated string, prints it word-wrapped in the text panel ($28A2), and returns past the string. Called through the jump table at $201E and directly.

Sets up the interrupts: CIA interrupts off and acknowledged, the video chip's raster interrupt on, the stage counter $B0 and text state cleared, the per-state hook set ($2D38 with X = 0), the first raster line from $299F, and the NMI, reset and IRQ vectors at $FFFA-$FFFF copied from $2944 (NMI and reset $294A, IRQ $2967).
NMI, reset and IRQ vectors copied to $FFFA: $294A, $294A, $2967.
The NMI handler, reached by the RESTORE key. Ignores an NMI from a CIA 2 timer, and returns unless $76 is zero and the game state $0F is not zero; then restarts the game at the warm start ($2067).

The raster interrupt: acknowledges it, takes the routine for the current stage ($B0, 0-2) from the table at $2999, moves the stage on, sets the raster line for the next stage from $299F (lines 10, 169, 185), and calls the routine. A, X and Y are kept.
The three raster stages: $29B1 (line 10, the room), $2A8B (line 169, the message bar), $2ACC (line 185, the text panel).
Part of irq_stages ($2999), read by $297C.
Raster lines of the three stages: 10, 169, 185.
JMP ($AE): calls the stage routine.
Sprite bits for the four sprite pairs (sprites 0+1, 2+3, 4+5, 6+7), the same with those bits clear, and each pair's register offset (0, 2, 4, 6).
Part of pair_masks ($29A5), read by $2A1D.
Part of pair_masks ($29A5), read by $2A29.

Raster stage 0, at line 10. Sets $D016 (multicolour, with the room's horizontal scroll $19 in play), black background, no X expansion, and the border colour: during a flash the count $0146 steps it through the colours at $2EAD. On the title (state 0) it sets up the title's video ($2BDE), runs its sprite and colour work ($2CEE, $2C4A, $8015, $804E) and the common end. In play it sets the room's character set ($D018 = $F0) and colours ($5D, $5E), and places the four characters' sprite pairs from the slot tables ($0244 the pair, $0208/$0210/$0218 the position, $0220 the colour, $0228/$0230 the two shape pointers, $1EAF the shape type), then jumps through the hook at $0124.
Loops over the four character slots, 3 down to 0, giving each its sprite pair.
Places a slot's two sprites one above the other: same X, the second 21 lines lower.
Next slot; after the last, jumps through the per-state hook at $0124.

The common end of raster stage 0: writes the sprite enable and X high bits gathered in $B2/$B3, makes every sprite multicolour, puts the sprites in front of the background in play ($D01B = 0) and behind it on the title ($FF), runs the door and room animation ($2C57), the message bar ($2B21), the text panel ($2812), and reads the joystick ($2200).

Raster stage 1, at line 169: after a short delay turns all sprites off, sets the message bar's fine scroll from $012E, the panel's character set ($D018 = $F2) and a blue background. Below state 10 it counts frames: $1E68 to 60, then $1E69 to 60, then $1E6A.
Inside irq_bar ($2A8B); the address is named only as the operand of a BIT at $80C3 that skips a LDA #$2A.

Raster stage 2, at line 185: after a short delay sets 38-column multicolour text, the panel's character set, black background and the panel's colours; shows the pointer (sprite 4, $24C3) when $56 is negative; then, for game states 0-8, jumps to the state's handler from the table at $2B0F.
The game state handlers run from the third raster stage, by $0F: 0 title ($2C00), 1 ($2680), 2 ($34FE), 3 ($315F), 4 ($33E9), 5 ($8051), 6 ($33E9), 7 ($35E8), 8 ($8075).
Part of state_handlers ($2B0F), read by $2B07.

Scrolls the message bar (screen rows 15 and 16) left two pixels a frame ($012E, the fine scroll stage 1 sets), and one column every fourth frame, while there is text to show (the line buffer's length $012D) or blank columns to clear ($0144). Each new character from the line buffer at $0400 (position $0130) is drawn at column 39 two rows high: letters as two characters, (letter - $41) times 2 plus $80 on top and that plus 1 below, and punctuation as its own pair. At the end of the line it sets $1E6B to $FF (the line free for the next speaker), empties the buffer unless on the title, and leaves 41 columns of blanks to scroll on.
Title video: screen on, sprite multicolours 14 and 15, background multicolour 14, no scroll, no sprite expansion, $D018 = $F0.

Game state 0 handler, the title: calls $8012; every third call steps the colour of the copyright row ($D832, 22 cells) through the table at $2C2C; moves the title's sprites ($2362) and calls $2E5C and $802A.
Colours the copyright line cycles through, ending with $FF.
X moves to the next colour of the table at $2C2C, back to the start at the $FF end; A is that colour.
Waits until the raster has passed line $43 and sets $D016 to $10.
Runs one of four animation jobs in turn each frame ($02A3, 0-3; addresses split low at $2C7B and high at $2C7F): $2C83, $8021, $2CC2, $8021. Not on the title, in state 5 or in states 10 and above.
Low bytes of the four animation jobs.
High bytes of the four animation jobs.

Animation job 0, every fourth frame: copies one of three 8-byte frames from $E800 (in the order 0, 1, 2, 1) over character 97 of the room's character set ($4308). Every tenth time it counts $68, and when that reaches 75 it adds a minute to the clock ($2570): 4 x 10 x 75 = 3,000 frames, one minute at 50 frames a second.
Animation job 2: calls $8072, then on every other call copies 24 bytes from a 40-byte ring at $E818, starting 4 bytes further on each time, over characters 52-54 of the room's set ($41A0).

Title sprites: places the eight sprites from the slot tables ($0208 X, $0210 X high, $0218 Y, kept at $94 or above the panel), white, shape $5A, or shape $EC/$ED (by the sprite's number) once a sprite has reached the panel; all eight on and multicolour, behind the background on the title.
Sets the hook at $0124 that the end of raster stage 0 jumps through, to entry X of the table at $2D48.
The hooks: $2A68 (none), $2D50, $2DC1, $8063.
Part of state_hooks ($2D48), read by $2D41.

Hook 1: calls $8069, then places sprites 0-2 side by side at line $85, 24 pixels apart, from the position $1D55/$1D4B less the room's scroll $C2/$C3, brown, with shapes $D5, $D4, $D3, and goes on to $8063.

Hook 2: works out a column from the position $1D55/$1D4B, rounds it to a step of 6 columns (or that plus 3), and when it is below 41 places sprites 0 and 1 there at line $72, brown, with shapes from $E8C0/$E8C3 (the next pair when $C8 is 2 or more); then the common end at $2A68.

For each title sprite that has reached the panel (Y $95 or more), redraws its shape at $7B40 or $7B80 so that only the part above the panel shows: the rows below are cleared and the rest copied from $5680.
Byte offsets of sprite shape rows, 3 bytes a row.
The border colours of a flash, seven steps, read by irq_room ($29CD) as $0146 counts down.

A main-loop task: finds, among the objects of the player's room (the list at $0250, $02F6 of them, with their rectangles in $1B00/$1B20/$1B40/$1B60), the nearest one on each side of the player's position ($64, and $1D7D) and stores their edges in $1DE4-$1DE7 and their positions in the room's list (the index into $0250) in $1DE8-$1DEB, all copied to $1DEC-$1DF3.

Builds the list of the objects in the player's room ($48): from the lists at $1C40, one for each room and each ended by a negative byte, it copies each object's number to $0250, its offset in the lists less the room number (its index among every room's objects) to $025A and a value from $E880 to $0264; $02F6 is the count. Also reached through the jump table at $202D.

Works out the room's scroll position in pixels ($C2/$C3, from the scroll column $40 and the fine scroll $19), then fills the four sprite slots with the characters (player included, $1D41-$1D4A) who are in the player's room ($48) and within the visible width: X position ($0208/$0210), Y ($0218, and $0240 for sorting), colour ($0220), the two shape pointers ($0228/$0230) and the shape type ($1EAF). At most four. It then gives the slots their sprite pairs ($0244) in order of Y, taking the smallest Y first: the character highest on the screen gets pair 3.

Puts the nine characters in their starting rooms (the table at $30B1) and clears their state: positions, counters and delays; X coordinate $A0, depth $1A, $1E06 = $FF (no walk target), $1DF4 = 2, $1EB4 = 10; and their screen positions ($3090). Clears $76 and $1E4E.
Screen position of character X from its room coordinates: $1D60 (Y, from $81 less the depth $1D7E plus $1E92) and the 9-bit X $1D4C/$1D56 (twice the depth plus $1D74/$1D6A).
The starting room of each of the nine characters.

The pick-up step of the investigation menu (game states 4 and 6). When $1E64 is 1, with the object number in A, counts what is carried through $8048: at 5, "YOU CAN/T CARRY ANY MORE!"; objects $24 and $25 go to $805D; others are marked carried ($1DAC = $80) and the menu goes on through $805A and $802D. With none, sets $0271 and opens the next menu ($800C, state 3).

What fire does in the menu states. In state 2 (playing) it opens the investigation menu ($34E9, then state 3). In states 3, 4 and 6, with an icon under the pointer ($0147) that the icon table at $1E5A allows, it carries out the icon: states 4 and 6 through $30BA; state 3 runs $800F with the icon, in state 2 for the while.
Sets the game state $0F to 2 (play).
Prints "*YOU CAN/T CARRY ANY MORE!".
Text printed in the text panel by the call at $313F: "(clears the panel) YOU CAN/T CARRY ANY MORE!  (new line)".
The end of say_cant_carry, after its text.

Game state 3 handler, the investigation menu, every frame. Shows the pointer (sprite 0, shape $5B) at $013B-$013D and the highlight ($3346). The pointer moves with momentum: every fourth frame the stick changes its speed $013E/$013F by one, within -8 to 7 in each direction; every sixth frame the speed falls by one towards zero; the pointer bounces off the edges of the icon box (X 244-305, Y $C0-$E1), its speed reversed. Its colour cycles ($2C40). Then it finds the icon under it ($33A3) and runs the adventure module's step ($801B) and $3722.
Calls $801B and goes on to $3722. Also reached through the jump table at $2027.
Draws the frame round the panel's picture box on the right of screen rows 17-24 (characters $0F, $13, $0D and corners $0C, $0E, $10, $11, in orange) and clears its inside ($32B4).
Fills the inside of the box, rows 18-23 and columns 27-37, with character $12 in light red.

Draws X icons in the box, each three characters wide and two rows high, codes from $C0 up, brown, three to a row at columns 27, 31 and 35 from row 18 (read from the screen with six icons drawn, 1 November 2026); then puts the pointer at X $F0, Y $C8, still, with no icon chosen ($0147 = $FF). Reached through the jump table at $2009.
Puts three consecutive character codes (X up) at ($D1),Y on, brown.
When an icon is under the pointer ($0147), places sprite 1 (shape $5C) over it from the tables at $3388/$3391/$339A and flashes its colour between black and white every five frames.
X position of the highlight for each of the nine icon places.
Bit 8 of the highlight's X for each icon place.
Y position of the highlight for each icon place.

Finds which icon place the pointer is over: the box is three rows by three columns of icons, 32 pixels apart across (from X $EE) and 16 down (from Y $BE), with a margin round each. Sets $0147 to the place (0-8) when it is one of the $0148 icons drawn, else $FF.

Game state 4 and 6 handler: a list in the box rather than icons. Four wide sprites (shapes $CE-$D0) mark the chosen line across the panel at the pointer's Y, their colour stepping through $34D9. Up and down on the stick (each new press, $1E65) move the choice $0147 within the $0148 entries; in state 6 the list scrolls ($6A) to keep the choice among six lines shown, with sprite 4 as a "more" arrow when there are lines below. Fire acts through $3258; left or right leaves the list (choice $FF) and, for the menus that set $1E64 to 3 or to 8 or 9, clears bit 7 of $1E33 for the character being questioned ($74).
Sixteen colours the menu marker and the pointer step through.
A = 1 when one of the nine characters is in the player's room ($48), else 0; also in $20.

Game state 2 handler, play, every frame. A main-loop task. When the room has been drawn and the player is in the room held in $77, clears $77, calls $8078 and holds the game in state 8 until something changes the state.

Unpacks picture record X of the list at $C100 into the room map, with the RAM under the I/O area switched in ($01 = $34). The picture's 15 rows are unpacked one after another, each from its left column to its right ($3C3D).
Puts $01 back to $35 and returns.

Next character of a packed picture. The stream is read a bit at a time, low bit first ($3D56).
Sets up room type A: silences voice 2 with the value saved in $1ED2, sets the raster stage 0 hook from the table at $3C8A, and calls $8066 for the types marked with bit 7 there.

Copies 72 bytes of the safe's picture, set X of the three at $E900, $E948 and $E990, over characters 35-43 of the room's character set ($4118).

One step of a portrait's appearance on the title: masks 127 bytes of the sprite shapes at $58C0 with the masks at $0C80 and $0C00 and the picture through ($BB), moves $BB on by 128 and the sprite up a line.

The title's cast introduction, every frame: in its phases ($1E66) shows the portrait sprites 0 and 1 at the right of the panel with the colours of the character being introduced (tables at $8C81-$8C94, read as $8C7B,X and $8C85,X with X 6-15), animates the portrait ($1E4E, $1E4F), starts the next character's picture ($8D13) every eight counts of $1E69, and at phase $FE builds the next portrait's masks ($8D6E).
The base of the indexed load LDA $8C7B,X at $8BC6, which runs with X 6 and up and so reads the portrait colours from $8C81; the address itself lies in the code.
Colours for the title's portraits, sprite colour and multicolour for each phase.
Part of portrait_colours ($8C81), read by $8BCF and $8C57.
Part of portrait_colours ($8C81), read by $8C6C.

Part of portrait_colours ($8C81), read by $8C7A.
The end of title_cast_step ($8CC8): $1E66 = $FF, the cast introduction is over.
Steps the title's cast phases ($1E66, up to 31) every third frame; phases 2-6 wipe the portrait on ($8B01); phases 21, 22 and 0 set a long delay.
The first sprite shape of each of the ten characters' portraits.

Moves to the next of the ten characters ($1E67) and builds the masks for its portrait: from its two sprite shapes (at the bank address of shape $8D09,x and the one after) through the table at $0E00 into $0C00 and $0C40.
Turns the masks at $0C00 into the second mask at $0C80 through $0D00, and resets the portrait's position and phase.
Sixteen bytes used to build the table at $0D00.
Offsets used when the title sets up the portraits.
Builds the title's tables at $0D00 and $0E00 (256 bytes each, from each byte's bit pairs), then works on the pictures at $5780 into $0F00 with the offsets at $8DA0.
Stores the byte $2E into the portrait buffer at ($28): offset from the table at $8DA0, plus $40 past entry 21, plus $42.
The ten biographies the title shows, in cast order with Snide first ("INSPECTOR SNIDE:" ... "MR DINGLE: FAMILY SOLICITOR. HERE TO READ THE WILL."), zero-terminated.
Clears the text panel and prints the biography of character $1E67 (string X of the list at $8E65). Reached through $8039.

Mirrors a character's sprite shapes while $76 counts down: each call does 127 bytes (two shapes), each byte through the pixel-reversal table at $0500 and the bytes of each row in reverse order (table $0380). With $76 negative it copies shapes instead, 63 bytes of each 64-byte step from ($BB) to ($BD), until $76 reaches $7F, and then sets $76 = 5.
The low byte of the operand of LDY $AAAA,X at $9160, rewritten by $9145.
The high byte of the operand of LDY $AAAA,X at $9160; $914E rewrites it (and $9145 the low byte) before the instruction runs.
Builds the tables at $0380 (for each of the 63 bytes of a sprite shape, the offset of the byte that mirrors it in its row: 2, 1, 0, 5, 4, 3, ...) and $03C0 (the same plus $40).
Picks a character's walking pose from what its movement does ($B6, 0-3).
For each room type, a depth that $935F compares with a character's ($1D7E) when it chooses the character's pose.

Starts mirroring character X's sprite shapes to match its new direction: marks it ($1E33 bit 2), points $BB at its shapes (tables $9216/$921F) and $BD at the buffer $58C0, notes the flip in $3FF0,x, and sets $76 = $89. While another flip is running, only marks the character to wait (bit 3).
Low byte of the address of each character's sprite shapes.
High byte of the address of each character's sprite shapes.
First shape offset for each pose.
Second shape offset for each pose.
First sprite shape of each of the nine characters.
Shape offsets for an eight-step animation: $9241 takes the step's offset into $B7 for the cast's poses, and the title's portraits use it too ($8C03).

Moves the cast, twice in every four frames (animation jobs 1 and 3, $8021): steps the animation counters $1E4E/$1E4F; for each character not paused (bit 7 of $1E33) and not the one speaking, moves it by its direction ($1DF4) through the tables at $93B3 (X low), $93B8 (X high) and $93BD (depth), updates its screen position, climbs or descends it towards the height it wants ($1E18 against $1E92), walks it towards its target ($1DFD/$1E06/$1E0F) and chooses its direction and walking pose, and starts a flip ($91E0) when it turns.
X step for each direction (low byte).
X step for each direction (high byte).
Depth step for each direction.
Shape offsets for the speaking character's animation.
The character speaking gets its talking shapes, which change with the animation step.

Puts every character's sprite shapes back the right way round (mirroring those $3FF0 marks flipped), clears their movement and flags, sets their shapes to the standing pose, and restarts their scripts ($A7E6). Reached through $8024.

Starts one of two tunes: entry $945E (through $8078) the one whose three voice addresses are at $97FB, entry $9461 (through $8027, at start-up) the one at $97F5; the BIT at $9460 hides the second entry's LDX. Copies the voices' sequence addresses to $1ED3, clears the voices' counters, sets the SID's 25 registers from $9801, and starts the player ($C1 = $A0, $1D05, $0138).
Points $4C/$4D at voice X's SID registers ($D400, $D407 or $D40E).
Register offsets of the three voices.
Turns a note byte into a SID frequency in $0139/$013A: the low four bits pick one of twelve values at $97DD, bits 4-6 how many times it is halved.
Reads the next byte of voice X's sequence, looping back to the start at $FF; returns it in A and Y.

One frame of voice X: ends the gate after its countdown ($1D18), glides the frequency towards its target ($1CFE/$1D01 to $1D09/$1D0C by $1D01's step), counts down the note ($1CEE), and reads the next command when it ends.

Reads and carries out voice X's next sequence byte: below $F0 a note ($96D7); from $F0, a command by its low four bits: 0, for voice 0 sets $1D1B and reads on, for the others waits; 1, the next byte is a note to glide to; 2, vibrato on; 3, the voice's control register cleared (silent); 4, its waveform without the gate (release); 5, flips bit 0 of its flags ($1CFB); 6, a rest of a note's length; 7, the next byte is a repeat count, or a negative byte loops back to the repeat's start; 8, the next byte chooses an instrument (envelope, filter routing, waveform, flags, from the tables at $981B-$9845); 9, a note set at once, then a glide to the next.
Sets voice X's frequency from the note byte (through $94C4) and gates it with its waveform.
Starts a note's length: 12 frames, or 6 when the note byte has bit 7 set; and its gate time, and a fresh pulse width.

Writes voice X's frequency for this frame, with the vibrato offset from the tables at $97B5/$97C9 when the voice's vibrato is on, or the alternating value $1D04 into its pulse width when its flag bit 0 is set.
Writes voice X's current frequency to its SID registers.

The music player, once a frame while a tune plays ($0138): updates the three voices ($9517), sets the filter routing, steps the vibrato and the alternating value, and sets the filter cutoff; then the pulse-width sweep ($977F).
For each voice with bit 7 of its flags set, narrows its pulse width ($1D1E) by 3 each frame. Reached through $804E.

The music player's tables: filter routing bits for the three voices, vibrato offsets, the twelve note frequencies (at $97DD), the two tunes' voice addresses (at $97F5), the SID's starting registers (at $9801), and the instruments' waveform, envelope and filter values (at $981B-$9845).
Part of music_tables ($97B2), read by $9713.
Part of music_tables ($97B2), read by $9718.
The twelve note frequencies of the top octave, two bytes each, read by note_frequency ($94CA).
Part of music_tables ($97B2), read by $94D0.
The two tunes' voice addresses, six bytes each (low bytes, then high bytes), read by play_tune ($9465).
Part of music_tables ($97B2), read by $94A1.
Attack and decay of each instrument (voice register 5), set by command $F8 ($9662).
Sustain and release of each instrument (voice register 6, $9668).
Bit 0: whether each instrument goes through the filter ($9676).
How long each instrument keeps its gate on ($968A, to $1CF8).
Each instrument's waveform ($9690, to $1D06).
Each instrument's pulse width high bits (voice register 3, $966F).
Each instrument's flags ($9696, to $1CFB): bit 0 the alternating pulse, bit 1 a filter setting, bit 7 the pulse sweep.
The return of pickup_sound in rooms of type 3 or 7, where it makes no sound.

A sound on voice 1, made with a delay loop that holds the game: a sweep of 110 frequencies taken from the program's own bytes at $2001-$206E, with the pulse width narrowing, about 110 steps. Not in rooms of type 3 or 7. Reached through $802D.
Starts a footstep: voice 1 noise at frequency $0808, filtered.
Ends the footstep's gate.
Silences voice 1.
The footstep's countdown ($02A6, set to 4 when the player takes a step): on, gate off, silence. Reached through $8030 every frame of play.
A door's sound on voice 1: two noisy bursts with delays between, filtered, then a lower tone left to fade ($1DA7 = $90).
The last part of the door's sound, played alone for sound 2.
A delay of X times 256 counts.
Sound 3: a low note on voice 1, noise, left to fade.
A main-loop task: plays the sound asked for in $1DA6 (1 the door, 2 its last part, 3 the low note) through the table at $99BA, or counts down $1DA7 and silences voice 1 when it ends.
The three sounds' routines.
Part of sound_table ($99BA), read by $99AF.
Stores A in $C1 and the SID's filter routing register.
A main-loop task: while the Major (character 7) is in the player's room, every 54 x 80 passes prints one of his four lines at $85F3, chosen at random ($99DF).
Prints one of the Major's four lines, chosen by two bits of $99F0.
A pseudo-random byte made from the frame counters, the fine scroll, the raster line, a character's X, a byte of the program and the background colour.
Prints the description of object $0271 (string X of the list at $9A47), or "YOU FIND NOTHING OF INTEREST." when it has none.
Text printed in the text panel (through $201E) by the call at $9A1D: "YOU FIND NOTHING OF INTEREST.".
The rest of examine_object ($9A0D), after the text at $9A20.
What Examine says about each object, in object order, zero-terminated ("HIGHEST QUALITY, WITH A FURRY COVER", ...); an empty string for an object with nothing to say.
The object descriptions ($9A47) go on here.
The read action: finds object $0271 in the list at $9EA1 (records of an object number and a zero-terminated text, ended by a negative byte) and prints its text.
What Read shows for each readable object: the will, the newspaper cutting, the note, the letter, the books and others.
The readable texts at $9EA1 go on here, past the edge of the memory map at $A000.

The consume action: object $0D, "YUK.. THAT DIDN/T TASTE TOO GOOD..!" and the player's colour changes to green ($1EB3 = 5); object 7, "<you> GASP IN AGONY AND DROP DEAD" and the end ($2033); anything else, "IT/S EMPTY..".
Text printed in the text panel (through $201E) by the call at $A177: "IT/S EMPTY..  (new line)".
The rest of consume_object ($A16D), after the text at $A17A.
Text printed in the text panel (through $201E) by the call at $A189: "YUK.. THAT DIDN/T TASTE TOO GOOD..!  (new line)".
The rest of consume_object ($A16D), after the text at $A18C.
"<you> GASP IN AGONY AND DROP DEAD", with word tokens.

The time/pause action: prints "THE TIME IS NOW:" and the clock, "PAUSED..PRESS FIRE TO CONTINUE.", and waits for fire with the game state shifted right and its top bit set (state 10 or more): anim_rotate ($2C5D) then skips the animation jobs, the clock's among them, so the clock stops.
Text printed in the text panel (through $201E) by the call at $A1E0: "(clears the panel)   THE TIME IS NOW: (new line)  (new line)".
The rest of time_pause ($A1E0), after the text at $A1E3.

The rest of time_pause ($A1E0), after the text at $A20E.

The rest of use_action ($A245), after the text at $A248.

The rest of use_object ($A253), after the text at $A258.
Puts the game in state 4 (a list menu) with the first entry chosen.

The rest of use_with ($A292), after the text it prints.

Finds the record for the verb $72, the object $C6 and the target $73 among the five-byte records at $A3ED (ended by a negative byte), runs its routine and says "OKAY."; with none, "SORRY, YOU CAN/T DO THAT.".
Points $26 at entry $48 (the player's room) of the room name list at $A362.

Says where the player is: by the room's entry at $A362, "YOU ARE OUTSIDE", "YOU ARE ON THE LANDING.", "YOU ARE IN <character>'S ROOM." or "YOU ARE IN <name>"; an entry of 1 says nothing. Reached through $8057 after each room change.
Text printed in the text panel (through $201E) by the call at $A2FE: "YOU ARE".
The rest of say_where ($A2EE), after the text at $A301.
Text printed in the text panel (through $201E) by the call at $A314: "IN   (new line)".
The rest of say_where ($A2EE), after the text at $A317.
Text printed in the text panel (through $201E) by the call at $A32A: "OUTSIDE  (new line)".
The end of say_where for an entry of 1: it says nothing.
Text printed in the text panel (through $201E) by the call at $A337: "ON THE LANDING.".
The rest of say_where ($A2EE), after the text at $A33A.
Text printed in the text panel (through $201E) by the call at $A353: "/S ROOM.".
The end of say_where after "<name>/S ROOM.": a carriage return ($A325).

The room list for "YOU ARE ...", one zero-terminated entry per room 0-29: a name ("THE DRAWING ROOM", "THE LIBRARY", "THE KITCHEN", "THE CELLAR", "THE HALL", "THE STUDY", "YOUR ROOM"), or a code: 1 says nothing (passages and stairs), 2 "OUTSIDE", 3 "THE LANDING", 4 and a character number "<name>/S ROOM" (rooms 7, 11, 12, 16-19, 21, 22). A character number of 0 is the entry's own terminator.
The use action's records, five bytes each: a verb, an object, a target and the routine to run; ended by a negative byte.

The cast's script interpreter, run once per pass of the main loop (task $803C). Each call serves the next of the nine characters in turn ($1E9B, 0-8; the counter $CA goes up each time it wraps). A character with a delay count in $1E9C,x waits, the count going down on every other turn. Otherwise, when its movement state lets it ($1E18,x negative, or equal to $1E92,x, and $1E06,x negative), the next instruction is fetched from the character's script pointer ($1E6D,x / $1E76,x): the opcode is the low five bits of its first byte, the operand length comes from the table at $A4FE ($FF: a zero-terminated string follows), the pointer is moved past the instruction and the handler from the table at $A4C8 is jumped to with ($2A) pointing at the instruction. A handler that needs to repeat the instruction puts the pointer back from $2A ($A542).
The interpreter's 27 opcode handlers, by opcode 0-26.
Part of script_ops ($A4C8), read by $A4C0.
Operand length of each of the 27 script opcodes, in bytes after the opcode byte; $FF means a zero-terminated string.

Script opcode 0, one operand: wait. On the first turn it sets bit 4 of $1E88,x and loads the count $1E45,x from the operand (through $A80D); the count goes down once every 16 interpreter rounds (when the low four bits of $CA are zero), and the instruction repeats until it reaches zero.
Puts the character's script pointer back to the instruction being run ($2A/$2B), so it runs again on the character's next turn.

Script opcode 1, three operands: stores the first in $1DFD,x, the second in $1E06,x and the third in $1E0F,x, and counts the change in $1E2A,x. The same three tables are set from a door's record by opcode 5.
The end of op_set_target: stores A in $1E0F,x and counts the change in $1E2A,x; also used by op_walk_to_room ($A660).
Script opcode 2, a two-byte operand: continues the character's script at that address. Also the shared jump of the conditional opcodes.
Script opcode 3, no operand: sets $1E18,x to $40 and waits until $1E92,x is $40 too; then puts the character in room 8 at $1D74/$1D6A/$1D7E = 1, $50, $0A.
Sets the character's room $1D42,x to A, and its $1E92,x and $1E18,x to $18 for room 8, else 0.
Works out the character's screen position from its room coordinates: $1D60,x (from $7F less $1D7E,x and $1E92,x) and the 9-bit $1D4C/$1D56,x (twice $1D7E,x plus $1D74/$1D6A,x).
Script opcode 4, no operand: a character in room 8 is moved to room 9 at 0, $20, $2A; then $1E18,x is cleared and the instruction waits until $1E92,x is zero.

Script opcode 5, one operand, a room number: looks through the 32 door records at $1F00 (8 bytes each, a room at +0 and +2) for one between the character's room and the target. Found, it sets the character's walk target ($1DFD/$1E06/$1E0F,x) to that door's position on this side and remembers the door in $1E7F,x. Not found, it flashes the screen red and prints "GUEST ERROR..".
Flashes the border and background red, prints "GUEST ERROR.." for the character being run, and puts the colours back: the script asked for a door that does not exist, or used one it had not chosen.
Text printed in the message bar, as speech by the call at $A625: "GUEST ERROR..".
The rest of guest_error ($A618), after "GUEST ERROR..": the colours back to black.
Turns a door's packed position (A, and $30) into room coordinates: $23 from the room's table at $1C00 when bit 1 of A is set, else from $1BE0 plus 2; $22/$21 from $30 times 8 plus $16.

Script opcode 6, a string: when the character is in the player's room ($48) it waits until the speech line is free ($1E6B negative) and then speaks the string through $85BD; in another room it does nothing.
Script opcode 7, a string: printed (through $2015) only when the character is in the player's room.
Script opcode 26, a string: printed through $2015 wherever the character is. Also the end of opcodes 7 and 22.
Script opcode 8, a two-byte address: jumps there when no other member of the cast and not the player is in the character's room.
Continues the script at the address in $26/$27: the jump taken by the conditional opcodes.
Script opcode 9: a character number (0 is the player, 1-9 the cast, read from $1D41) and an address: jumps when that character is in this character's room.
Script opcode 10: a character number and an address: jumps when that character is not in this character's room.
Script opcode 11, a two-byte address: jumps to 6502 code there, which returns to the interpreter's caller.
Script opcode 12, one operand: stores it with bit 7 set in $1E7F,x, as the door to use.
Script opcode 13: a number and an address: with a door chosen (bit 7 of $1E7F,x), jumps when the door's number equals $1DAC indexed by the first operand; without one, prints GUEST ERROR.
Script opcode 14, an object number: marks the object as held by this character ($1DAC,object = character + $81).

An opcode handler that no entry of the table at $A4C8 names: it reads an object number and an address (JSR $A820), and branches back to $A731 (an RTS) while the object's place ($1DAC) is not negative. Its last instruction, BPL $A731, ends at $A73A, just before the shared jump at $A73B.
JMP to goto_26 ($A6DE): the jump taken by opcodes 13 and 24 when their test holds.
Script opcode 24: a room and an address: jumps when that room is the one in $1D41, character 0's room in the numbering opcode 9 uses (the player's).
Script opcode 25: a character number and an address: sets that character's script pointer.

Script opcode 17, no operand, and opcode 15 at $A759, an address: go through the door in $1E7F,x. If its record's bit 1 at +4 is set (locked), opcode 17 repeats (waits) and opcode 15 jumps to its address. Otherwise it marks the door used (bit 0); when three or more of the cast are already in the far room and fewer than three in this one it waits, and otherwise it moves the character to the far side at the door's position there; it redraws the door through $2021 when the door is one on screen ($1CDE, $4A entries).
Script opcode 15's entry, an address: as opcode 17 ($A756) with A = 0, so that when the door is locked the script jumps to the address instead of waiting.
Script opcode 18, an address: jumps when the low bit of $99F0's result is clear.

Points each character's script at its start in the table at $A7FB. The loop runs Y from 9 to 0, so it sets ten pointers from a table of nine: the tenth is read from $A80D-$A80E, the first bytes of the routine after the table.
The script start of each of the nine characters, character 0 first.
Part of script_starts ($A7FB), read by $A7F1.
Reads the instruction's first operand into $2E and A.
Reads the two-byte operand after the opcode into $26/$27.
Reads the word at operand bytes 2-3 into $26/$27 and the first operand into $2E and A.
A = $1BE0 indexed by the character's room, Y kept.
A = $1C00 indexed by the character's room, Y kept.
A twin of room_table_1BE0 and room_table_1C00 for the room widths at $1C20 (with $22 cleared): A = the width of the character's room, Y kept. Nothing calls it.
Script opcode 16: an object number and a place: sets $1DAC,object to the place.
Counts the cast in room A (characters 1-9 in $1D41,y), into A and $42.
Finds the door record at $1F00 that joins the two rooms of the operand (either way round): X its number, Y its offset, carry set when found.
Compares A with the two rooms of the door record at Y (+0, +2): Z set when either matches.
Script opcode 19: two rooms: clears the locked bit of the door between them, and redraws it if on screen. GUEST ERROR if there is no such door.
Script opcode 20: two rooms: sets the locked bit of the door between them, and redraws it if on screen.
Script opcode 21: a value and an address: jumps when the value is no more than $C8.
Script opcode 22, a string: when the character is in the player's room, prints its name ($8568), a space and the string.

Script opcode 23, an address: when the character is in the player's room, sets its delay to $40 and prints the inline text at $A8E3 (".." and "MR. " and "/S BEEN STRANGLED!", with two word tokens between), then jumps to the address.
Text printed in the message bar, as speech by the call at $A8E0: "<INSPECTOR>..MR. <DINGLE>/S BEEN STRANGLED!".
The rest of op_strangled ($A8D2), after the text at $A8E3.

The Reverend's script (character 0), from the drawing room: wanders it at random, now and then belching (" BELCHES"); sometimes walks through room 1 to the library, waits, says "LOOKING FOR CLUES INSPECTOR?" and comes back.

Bentley's script (character 1), the butler. First " ADVANCES: "THIS WAY TO YOUR ROOM SIR"", and takes the player upstairs (room 8, then rooms 14, 25 and 15 to "YOUR ROOM"); then down again through room 1 to his room (7), unlocking and locking its door, "YOU/LL FIND NOTHING OF INTEREST IN HERE.."; asks the Reverend in the drawing room "IS EVERYTHING SATISFACTORY, SIR?"; and meets the Cook in room 13, going into her room (11) with her and locking the door for a long wait, unless the player is there ("AHEM").

The Cook's script (character 2), from the kitchen: "OOH YES I KNOW DEAR.." when Gabriel is there; walks out and back; in room 13 or her room (11), to the player "YOU/LL FIND YOUR ROOM UPSTAIRS..THIS ONE/S MINE."; waits there while Bentley is with her.
Inside the Cook's script. Named only by the placeholder operand of LDY $AAAA,X at $9160, which $9138 rewrites ($9161/$9162) before it runs.

Gabriel's script (character 3), the maid, from the kitchen: wanders the ground floor, "OH.." in the library, the study, her room (12): "WELL!" when its door will not open, "HELP!" when the way out is locked, "LET ME IN!" at the kitchen, "..DUM DE DAH..".

Cynthia's script (character 4), from her room (17): "GRIMACES..", " SNIFFS DISSAPROVINGLY.."; at Dingle's door (19) "SORRY..WRONG ROOM"; "HELLO.."; in room 20 "AWFUL WEATHER.."; in the Major's room (21) "TSK TSK..SUCH A MESS..".

Native code for Dingle's script (opcode 11): Cynthia (character 4) is killed in the hall (room 9): marked so ($AD18, state 3), given the body shapes $D1 and a place on the floor, object $1D put in the list at $1C60; then "<you> HEAR<a>SCREAM ..FOLLOWED ..." is printed ($ACC5).
